evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the stakeholder need (create a game and provide basic metadata) without prescribing UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete technical mechanism (invitation via URL) rather than just the need to invite estimators.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget (a single multi-line text field).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a stakeholder need (visibility of items) without implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the capability needed (select an item) without prescribing concrete UI or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the stakeholder need to add items; no UI widgets or technical mechanisms prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Focuses on the need to edit items rather than how editing must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to remove items without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the desired behavior (show estimates) without prescribing how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific aggregation algorithm (average) rather than stating the stakeholder need for an agreed estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specifies an automated implementation behavior (auto-fill under a specific condition) instead of the underlying need.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to record the agreed estimate without prescribing UI or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Requests the capability to re-estimate; does not prescribe how this must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete data source/format (spreadsheet) as the required mechanism rather than the need to bulk-add stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific manual import mechanism and data format (spreadsheet), which is a solution choice.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to find past games without prescribing UI or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States the need to view a transcript; no concrete implementation or format is mandated.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete file format (HTML) for export, which is an implementation/format choice.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific export format (CSV), which is a solution-level detail.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the intent to remove data; does not prescribe implementation details beyond the business need.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies required account information (data fields) as part of the stakeholder need; not an explicit UI/widget or low-level technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Describes the needed authentication capability (credentials) rather than prescribing a low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to update account details without prescribing how that must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Focuses on the business need to remove an account and related data rather than technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user-facing requirement (local time display) without prescribing specific implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the user's preferred communication channel for password reminders (email) as a stakeholder need rather than a low-level technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific numeric estimation sequences (concrete algorithm/choice) rather than the general need to choose an estimation scale.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Defines a business constraint (maximum participants) rather than prescribing technical implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete access/join mechanism (enter name on a URL page), which prescribes an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States the need to view the item being estimated without prescribing UI or technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a visibility need without constraining implementation.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the information need (who has given an estimate) without prescribing how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes the desired behavior (simultaneous reveal) as a need, not as a low-level solution.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the allowed interaction timing (change estimate until reveal) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Requests access to historical estimates; does not mandate a particular storage or UI mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States an informational need without prescribing how to present or store that information.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a user-facing capability (a two-minute timer) to limit discussion; it's a stakeholder need rather than low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired timer behavior to support the activity rather than prescribing internal implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a navigation/visibility need; 'scroll back' is a user action description rather than a low-level solution constraint.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a consistency expectation for the UI presentation, stated as a stakeholder need rather than a specific implementation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Specifies allowed interaction timing; does not prescribe how the functionality is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete UI element and presentation detail (small thumbnail near cards) rather than stating the need for personalization/identification generically.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technical standards for implementation (XHTML/CSS), which is an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Requests a glossary/definitions to support shared understanding; does not mandate a technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete implementation detail (database indexes) rather than stating a performance need.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete platform/browser support (implementation targets), which are solution-level constraints.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Mandates a specific set of implementation guidelines (W3C) rather than expressing the accessibility need at a stakeholder level.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a non-functional stakeholder need (performance) without prescribing how to achieve it.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode, so that I can use any language I like
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical/data encoding format (Unicode) rather than the higher-level need to support multiple languages.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user-facing expectation (URL predictability) as part of the user experience rather than mandating an internal technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Requests user-facing error presentation; does not prescribe specific implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: States a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) as a stakeholder need rather than prescribing a specific storage format or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Requests visibility into usage metrics; does not mandate specific metrics collection mechanisms or storage formats.
